ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Commercial Act (Act No. 1001), as amended, Articles 169-196 and 262-276; Act on Registration of Commercial Establishments (Act No. 12172), as amended; Act on Reporting and Use of Specific Financial Transaction Information, Articles 2, 5 and 8; Decree on the Operation of the Financial Intelligence Unit, as amended; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality; Foreign Exchange Transactions Act; Medical Devices Act for Class III ISIC 3250. The Korean UBO and AML/CFT regime is administered by the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit (KoFIU) under the Financial Services Commission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation of each corporate shareholder and each UBO entity owning above 25%
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent corporate registry in the shareholder's country of organization
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille states: local notarization if required and apostille issued by the designated competent authority, then certified Korean translation submitted to the Korean bank or registry; for non-member states: local notarization, authentication by local Ministry of Foreign Affairs, consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate, then certified Korean translation. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive alternative paths and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing for each foreign corporate investor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent company registry or statutory agency in the investor's home jurisdiction
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path under the Hague Convention if the issuing state is a member; otherwise consular legalization by the Korean diplomatic mission. Do not combine both. The certificate must be dated no more than 90 days before submission to the Korean Commercial Registry or a financial institution.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution or Power of Attorney appointing the Korean incorporation agent and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Board of directors of the foreign corporate shareholder, notarized by a local notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarize the resolution or PoA, then either apostille by the competent authority of the Apostille Convention state or consular legalization by the Korean Embassy or Consulate for non-member states. These paths are alternative, not cumulative; the Korean Consulate shall not receive an already-apostilled document for legalization.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association or Constitutional Documents of each corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate registrar or legalized extract from the company register
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For an Apostille state, certified copy from the registry with apostille; for non-member states, certified copy authenticated by the local Ministry of Foreign Affairs and then legalized by the Korean consulate. A certified Korean translation must accompany the document for filing with the Korean registry and banks.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter issued for each foreign shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: The bank letter must be signed by an authorized bank officer, notarized, and then either apostilled for member states or consular legalized for non-member states. Korean financial institutions under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act also require identification of the person opening the account and documentary proof of source of funds.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: The legal dossier must include mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, officers, UBOs, and authorized signatories against the Korean KoFIU watchlist, UN Security Council sanctions lists, OFAC SDN and non-SDN lists, and the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List. Enhanced due diligence must be performed for any PEP, foreign government official, or family or close associate of a PEP, including independent verification of source of wealth and source of funds, senior management approval, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Negative media and adverse regulatory database checks are required together with continuous sanctions-list screening for the life of the Yuhan Hoesa and before every wire or letter-of-credit transaction. All screening results must be documented and retained for at least five years under Korean AML/CFT reporting obligations.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: IROS - Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea at www.iros.go.kr
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Commercial Act and the Commercial Registration Act, the company name must be in Korean script. The entity type must be indicated as Yuhan Hoesa for a limited liability company. English or other foreign alphabets may be used only as a secondary transliteration or registered foreign name, not in place of Hangul. The four-tier naming convention is applied: first, a unique core name in Hangul; second, a business purpose description; third, the entity form suffix Yuhan Hoesa; and fourth, no misleading or prohibited sensitive tokens. The name must not be identical to an existing registered name in the same line of business nationwide, and phonetic equivalents in Hangul are treated as identical.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Because IROS does not operate a formal reservation, the name-search finding is operationally reliable for only 30 days; if incorporation is not completed within that window, a fresh search must be rerun. If the commercial registry registrar rejects the proposed name during incorporation filing, the applicant must first obtain a written statement of rejection grounds from the registry. Within two weeks, the applicant may file a written appeal for immediate administrative review with the head of the relevant district court registry office. If the registry office maintains the rejection, the applicant may petition for judicial resolution under the Non-Contentious Case Litigation Procedure Act, or withdraw the filing and submit a new registration with a revised name. The applicant should also provide a rebuttal memorandum demonstrating that the proposed name is not identical or deceptively similar to any prior registered Korean name in the same business category.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office or commercial mailbox is not permissible as the primary registered office of a Class III medical device manufacturing Yuhan Hoesa. The Medical Devices Act requires a physical manufacturing facility subject to pre-licensing and post-licensing on-site inspection by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety; the National Tax Service requires a physical place of business for VAT and corporate tax registration; and Korean financial institutions under the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act refuse account opening for entities with only virtual-office addresses. A virtual office may be used only as a secondary correspondence address after the manufacturing plant and principal registered address are licensed and registered.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist: (1) MFDS pre-license inspection of the manufacturing clean room, sterilization validation, and quality management system under KGMP; (2) unannounced National Tax Service field inspection during the first 12 months of VAT and corporate tax filing; (3) municipal fire and safety inspection of the registered physical premises; (4) local government industrial or commercial premises inspection; (5) post-license MFDS surveillance inspection every two years. Quantified risk: MFDS pre-license inspection is 100% required; unannounced NTS new-company inspection risk is

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of South Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Articles 287-2 through 287-2 (Limited Liability Company), Article 289 (Articles of Incorporation), Article 292 (Registration of Incorporation), Article 317 (Application for Registration of Incorporation), and Article 318 (Effective Date of Incorporation).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Court Registration Division of the District Court having jurisdiction over the principal office of the company (e.g., Seoul Central District Court Registration Division).
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation (법인설립등기신청서) together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and other required attachments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. The Commercial Act does not impose a minimum paid-up capital for a Yuhan Hoesa (LLC). However, for medical device manufacturing, the company must demonstrate sufficient financial resources to satisfy the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) licensing requirements, but no statutory minimum capital is mandated.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF [COMPANY NAME] (YUHAN HOESA) ADOPTED BY UNANIMOUS WRITTEN CONSENT IN LIEU OF A FIRST MEETING ON [DATE]

WHEREAS, the undersigned, being all of the directors of [Company Name] (the "Company"), a limited liability company organized under the laws of the Republic of Korea, do hereby consent to and adopt the following resolutions, which shall be effective as of the date hereof, in accordance with the Company's Articles of Incorporation and the Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea.

NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED:

1. Adoption of Articles of Incorporation. The Articles of Incorporation of the Company, as executed and notarized on [Date], are hereby ratified, approved, and adopted in their entirety. The registered office of the Company shall be located at [Full Address], Republic of Korea, and the Company shall maintain its principal place of business at such address.

2. Subscription and Payment of Share Capital. The initial share capital of the Company shall be [Amount] Korean Won (KRW), divided into [Number] shares of no par value. Each director hereby subscribes to the number of shares set forth opposite his/her name on the subscription list attached hereto. The full subscription price has been paid into the Company's designated bank account, and the directors acknowledge receipt of the capital contribution. The Company shall issue share certificates to each shareholder in accordance with the Articles of Incorporation.

3. Appointment of Statutory Officers. The following persons are hereby appointed to the offices indicated, to serve until their successors are duly elected and qualified:
   - [Name] as Chief Executive Officer (CEO) and Representative Director, with full authority to act on behalf of the Company in all matters, including but not limited to executing contracts, opening bank accounts, and representing the Company before governmental authorities.
   - [Name] as Chief Financial Officer (CFO) and Director, with authority to manage the Company's financial affairs, sign financial documents, and oversee accounting records.
   - [Name] as Director, with general supervisory duties.

4. Banking Authorization. The Company hereby authorizes the opening of bank accounts with [Bank Name] and any other financial institution as deemed necessary. The CEO and CFO are jointly and severally authorized to sign all banking documents, including account opening forms, deposit and withdrawal slips, and loan agreements, and to execute any related instruments on behalf of the Company.

5. Corporate Seal and Execution. The Company adopts a corporate seal, an imprint of which is affixed to the minutes of this resolution. The CEO is authorized to use such seal on all corporate documents, contracts, and instruments, and to delegate such authority as necessary.

6. Filing and Registration. The CEO and any director are hereby authorized to prepare, execute, and file all necessary documents with the competent Court Registration Division, the National Tax Service, and any other governmental agency to effectuate the incorporation of the Company and to obtain all required licenses and permits.

7. General Authority. The officers and directors are authorized to take any and all actions necessary or convenient to carry out the purposes of these resolutions, including the execution of any additional documents, the payment of fees, and the engagement of legal counsel or other advisors.

This resolution shall be effective immediately and shall remain in full force and effect until revoked by a subsequent resolution of the Board of Directors.

IN WITNESS WHEREOF, the undersigned directors have executed this resolution as of the date first written above.

[Signature of Director 1]
[Signature of Director 2]
[Signature of Director 3]

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Notarize Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public (공증인) and the Company's legal counsel
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a licensed Korean attorney to draft the Articles of Incorporation (정관) in compliance with the Commercial Act. The Articles must include the company name, purpose (including medical device manufacturing), registered office address, share capital, number of shares, and provisions for directors and officers. After drafting, the Articles must be notarized by a Korean notary public. The notary will verify the identity of the incorporators and the legality of the provisions. The notarized Articles are a prerequisite for registration. Ensure that the business purpose explicitly includes the manufacturing of Class III medical devices, specifically coronary drug-eluting stents, to align with future licensing requirements.
required_dossiers: Identification documents of all incorporators (passport or Korean ID)
Power of attorney if any incorporator is represented
Proof of registered office address (lease agreement or title deed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary raises objections, correct the Articles to comply with mandatory provisions and resubmit. If the notary requires additional documentation, provide it within 5 business days. If the Articles are rejected due to illegal purpose, revise the business scope and re-notarize.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Appoint Directors and Prepare Initial Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Incorporators and the Board of Directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After notarization, the incorporators must convene a meeting or execute a written consent to appoint the initial directors and officers. The board must adopt the pro-forma first board resolution as provided in the incorporation framework. This resolution must be signed by all directors and kept in the corporate records. The resolution should include the adoption of the Articles, subscription of shares, appointment of officers, and banking authorization. The minutes must be dated and retained for submission with the registration application. Ensure that the resolution is in Korean or bilingual, but the English version is for reference.
required_dossiers: Written consent or minutes of the board meeting
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any director fails to sign, obtain a separate written consent or hold a formal meeting. If capital deposit is not made, arrange for immediate payment and obtain a bank certificate. If the resolution is incomplete, amend and re-execute.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File Incorporation Registration with the Court
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Court Registration Division of the District Court with jurisdiction over the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for registration of incorporation (법인설립등기신청서) to the competent court. The application must be accompanied by the notarized Articles of Incorporation, the board resolution, proof of capital deposit, and identification of directors. The court will review the documents for compliance with the Commercial Act. Upon approval, the court will issue a Certificate of Registration (법인등기부등본). This certificate is the official proof of the company's legal existence. The registration fee must be paid via court stamps or electronic payment. The process typically takes 3-5 business days.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court issues a correction order, rectify the deficiencies within 10 days. If the application is rejected, file an appeal or reapply after correcting the issues. If the court requires additional evidence of capital, provide a fresh bank certificate. If the registered office is not verifiable, provide a lease agreement or utility bill.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Business Registration Certificate from National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) - Local District Tax Office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, the company must register for business tax purposes with the NTS within 20 days of incorporation. Submit the business registration application (사업자등록신청서) along with the Certificate of Incorporation, the company's corporate seal, and identification of the CEO. The NTS will issue a Business Registration Certificate (사업자등록증) which is required for opening bank accounts, issuing tax invoices, and conducting business. The registration is free of charge. The certificate will include the company's tax identification number.
required_dossiers: Identification of CEO (passport or Korean ID)
Power of attorney if filed by an agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the NTS queries the application, provide additional documentation such as a detailed business plan or proof of office. If the application is rejected, correct the errors and resubmit. If the office is not physically present, arrange for a virtual office or a registered agent.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Food and Drug Safety (MFDS) - Medical Device Division; also Ministry of Environment (MOE) for environmental permits
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing License (의료기기 제조업 허가) under Article 6 of the Medical Devices Act

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment (MOE) - Korea Environment Corporation (KECO)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Environmental Registration (신고) - Category 3 (Small-scale manufacturing) as per the Environmental Impact Assessment Act; however, if the facility exceeds certain thresholds (e.g., floor area > 1,000 m² or hazardous chemical usage), a Full EIA Report may be required. For a typical stent manufacturing facility, an Environmental Registration is likely sufficient.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: pH 5.8-8.6, BOD ≤ 50 mg/L, COD ≤ 40 mg/L, SS ≤ 50 mg/L, T-N ≤ 20 mg/L, T-P ≤ 2 mg/L (per Water Quality Conservation Act). VOCs: ≤ 10 ppm for toluene, ≤ 20 ppm for xylene (per Clean Air Conservation Act). Hazardous waste: Must be stored in approved containers and disposed of by licensed waste handlers; manifest system required.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certification from the National Fire Agency (NFA) - requires installation of fire suppression systems, emergency exits, and compliance with the Fire Services Act. Structural load inspections by the local government building authority to ensure the facility meets seismic and load-bearing standards. Occupational Safety and Health Administration (OSHA) approval from the Ministry of Employment and Labor (MOEL) - must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act, including workplace hazard assessments, personal protective equipment, and emergency response plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea - electronic portal: HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr); export customs clearance portal: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS (unipass.customs.go.kr).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the Yuhan Hoesa LLC: (1) The foreign investor lodges a Foreign Investment Promotion Act notification with KOTRA or the designated foreign exchange bank and funds the stated capital; (2) The entity completes incorporation under the Korean Commercial Act, executes articles of association, and appoints a domestic legal representative/tax agent; (3) Within 20 days of business commencement, the representative files the Application for Business Registration with the competent district tax office using the HomeTax portal or in person, under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act; the NTS then assigns a 10-digit Business Registration Number used as the unified TIN for VAT, corporate income tax, and withholding tax. (4) A foreign non-resident entity with no domestic fixed establishment is not VAT-registered; Korean-source income is handled through withholding by the local payor. If a fixed establishment is created later, the same Business Registration procedure is mandatory before supplies occur.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Korea does not operate a check-the-box regime; entity tax classification is driven by the Commercial Act and the Corporate Tax Act. The Yuhan Hoesa is mandatorily taxed at entity level on worldwide income. Anti-hybrid adjustment rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act apply automatically without taxpayer election.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary exemption threshold for corporations; VAT registration is mandatory from the date of business commencement under the Value-Added Tax Act. A Yuhan Hoesa LLC must always register as a general taxpayer; the KRW 80,000,000 simplified taxpayer threshold applies only to qualifying natural persons and does not apply to this entity.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Electronic tax invoices issued through the HomeTax electronic tax invoice system are mandatory for business taxpayers. Invoice data must be transmitted to the NTS in the e-invoice channel, generally no later than the following business day after supply. HomeTax open API and bulk XML submission are available for ERPs and billing systems. There is no physical stamp, but NTS runs real-time validation and anti-fraud matching of business registration numbers, tax invoice sequences, and cash receipts.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under the VAT Act is available where the Yuhan Hoesa physically exports the drug-eluting stent system outside the Republic of Korea under an accepted KCS export declaration, the sale contract and payment documentation show a non-resident overseas buyer, title and risk pass abroad, and export proceeds are repatriated through the required bank settlement process. Qualifying offshore services/intangible supplies to non-resident recipients can also be zero-rated if consumed outside Korea and supported by contract and evidence of remittance. Exporters may file for early VAT refund of input tax incurred on export supplies through HomeTax.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Korea Customs Service UNI-PASS Export Declaration (export customs clearance record)
Bill of Lading (ocean) or International Air Waybill (air cargo)
Zero-rated VAT Tax Invoice issued via HomeTax
Foreign Exchange Purchase/Export Proceeds Settlement Certificate issued by a designated foreign exchange bank under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act
SWIFT MT103 / Letter of Credit settlement record evidencing receipt from the overseas buyer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the export documentation bundle is incomplete, the NTS will reverse the zero-rating and assess VAT at 10% on the export consideration, plus statutory additional tax and interest under the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes. Fraudulent export declarations, fabricated tax invoices, or undocumented FX settlement may result in criminal penalties under the Punishment for Tax Evaders Act, forfeiture of refunds, and retrospective reassessment for the maximum statutory tax assessment period. The NTS coordinates with Korea Customs Service to verify the underlying physical export movement.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea (central bank), with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the principal foreign exchange administration authority under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a free-floating Korean won (KRW) with a fully convertible current account for trade settlements, services, and ordinary business remittances. The Foreign Exchange Transactions Act adopts a notification-based system rather than a blanket license requirement: current account transactions are generally unrestricted, while capital account transactions such as direct equity investment, overseas borrowing, and portfolio flows require prior filing, approval, or use of a designated foreign exchange bank. Export proceeds may be retained in foreign currency accounts and no mandatory conversion to KRW is imposed. Profit remittances such as dividends for a foreign-owned Yuhan Hoesa are legally permissible after the statutory corporate tax return and withholding tax clearance; however, remittance applications must be supported by audited financial statements, board resolutions, and tax payment certificates. The main hurdles are not convertibility caps but documentary proof of beneficial ownership, filing of the foreign investment notification through an authorized bank, KOTRA, or the Ministry of Economy and Finance, and compliance with FATF-aligned beneficial ownership reporting. In practice, banks apply enhanced due diligence to Class III medical device manufacturers and may reject transfers if the underlying commercial contract, shipping documents, and product certification are not consistent.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export settlement must be completed within the agreed contractual payment term, with a standard statutory benchmark of 90 days from the date of export declaration; longer periods require approval from a foreign exchange bank. Korea does not impose a mandatory conversion or surrender ratio on export proceeds; exporters are allowed to maintain the proceeds in domestic foreign-currency deposit accounts or convert them at market rates for KRW working capital.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Basic Operational Currency Account (KRW plus USD)
Foreign Currency Deposit Account and Operational KRW Account
FDI Settlement Account and Trade Service Account
Corporate Current Account with FX Hedging Facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Foreign fintech EMIs such as Wise, Revolut, and similar offshore digital financial institutions are not viable as primary or legal corporate treasury rails in South Korea. They are not licensed as banks or authorized foreign exchange dealers under the Banking Act, cannot issue or operate a domestic KRW corporate account, and cannot clear inbound FDI or outbound trade settlements under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act. Offshore EMIs may at most provide ancillary non-KRW expense cards, but their use is severely limited and they are not acceptable for FX exemption, capital verification, or KYC compliance evidence. Viability rating: Low.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Statutory directors who are Korean tax residents are generally required to physically attend a branch interview for a high-risk corporate account, providing a corporate seal registration certificate, business license, and personal identification. Non-resident overseas directors may be permitted to use a consular notarized power of attorney and locally appointed authorized signatory, but the responsible bank compliance committee still mandates either an in-person appearance or a secure real-time video KYC interview for account activation. Remote consular proxy opening is possible only where the bank accepts a nationally notarized and apostilled file, with the final AML interview held by video call; for Class III medical device manufacturers, many tier-1 banks require at least one physical executive appearance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO and indirect Korean shareholder opacity in the Yuhan Hoesa structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Beneficial Ownership Registry extract not older than three months, complete shareholders ledger, notarized and apostilled constitutional charter, passport and current address proof of every natural person holding 10% or more, and a clear organizational chart tracing all ownership to natural persons.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk Class III medical device manufacturer without proven local operating substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Valid medical device manufacturing license and GMP certificate issued by the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety, lease agreement with physical floor plan, utility invoices, equipment purchase invoices, payroll census, corporate certification standards for coronary drug-eluting stents, and audited financial statements for at least two fiscal periods.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of funds for the initial foreign capital injection into the escrow account
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Remitting entity bank statements for the last twelve months, detailed source-of-wealth statement, notarized board resolution authorizing the equity subscription, evidence that the remitting bank account is in the investor corporate name, and official tax payment or tax exemption certificates related to the injected funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unusual or high-risk trade distribution routes for drug-eluting stent exports
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed genuine commercial agreement with the overseas medical device buyer, commercial invoice, packing list, airway bill or bill of lading, certificate of origin, MFDS export approval, product registration evidence in the destination jurisdiction, distributor KYC questionnaire, product traceability records, and export control classification.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, the overseas investor must file a pre-investment notification online through Invest KOREA/KOTRA or at an authorized foreign exchange bank before remitting funds. The capital injection should be made by SWIFT MT103 from the investor's overseas corporate account to a temporary foreign currency escrow account opened at the designated domestic tier-1 bank. The FX remittance purpose code must identify direct equity investment, and the payment reference must include the Korean entity name and the foreign investment notification number. After the funds arrive, the designated bank issues the foreign investment certificate, the company completes capital verification through the registry of the Seoul court or relevant district court, and the tax office business registration is updated with the increased capital. No utilization of the escrowed funds is permitted until the certificate of foreign investment and finalized capital verification have been issued.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound disbursements for raw materials, machinery, licensing fees, and intercompany trade should be executed over SWIFT MT103 for open-account wire settlements, through commercial letters of credit using SWIFT MT700/MT710 for documentary trade, or through documentary collections under D/P and D/A terms. The corresponding foreign exchange bank will require the underlying commercial invoice, packing list, transport document, and a proper trade purpose code. For USD, EUR, or JPY settlements, the receiving bank details must be matched against the beneficiary account, and all payments must remain within the declared trade scope of the Yuhan Hoesa medical device manufacturing operation.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Corporate forward contracts transacted with a licensed domestic authorized foreign exchange bank to hedge trade receivables and payables, supported by real invoices and shipment evidence.
FX swap transactions for working capital cash-flow hedging and foreign-currency loan repositioning, limited to documented underlying exposure and with standard 12-month rollover discipline.

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts only to hedge approved underlying economic exposure through authorized onshore banks under Ministry of Economy and Finance reporting rules, not for speculative positions, and with strict enforcement of the real-demand principle.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting of Members and approval of annual financial statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company registered office and members; no government filing arises unless the meeting approval changes the articles of incorporation, directors, registered office or other registrable particulars.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, no later than March 31 of the following year.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct government filing fee; failure to convene the annual meeting and approve the financial statements within three months violates the Korean Commercial Act, exposes directors to civil liability for management discharge issues, and, for a dormant company, may support a court dissolution petition under Commercial Act Article 176.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax final return, including financial statements and supporting audit report where required
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) through HomeTax; the concurrent local corporate income tax surcharge is remitted to the competent local government.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months from the end of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year company, the normal deadline is March 31, subject to lawful extension where audited financial statements are pending or the return is prepared by a prescribed tax professional.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure-to-report surcharge of 20% of the underreported corporate tax plus daily delinquency interest currently at 0.022% per day; persistent non-filing permits NTS enforced collection, seizure of bank accounts and business assets, suspension of business operations, and proceedings toward administrative strike-off of the entity.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24% national corporate income tax plus a 10% municipal local income tax surcharge (26.4% combined top marginal rate); lower brackets: 9% on taxable income up to KRW 200 million, 19% on KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 21% on KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Foreign-invested high-technology medical-device enterprises may obtain a 100% corporate income tax exemption for five years and a 50% reduction for two further years under the Korean Foreign Investment Promotion Act; R&D expenditure tax credits are available under the Special Tax Treatment Control Act at up to 30% of eligible R&D expenses for fiscal 2024; free economic zone incentives and job-creation tax credits may also be claimed; Korea does not operate a separate patent box regime.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean corporate income tax return (Form 12) and annex schedules, e-filed through the National Tax Service HomeTax electronic filing portal at www.hometax.go.kr.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual final return; semi-annual preliminary corporate tax prepayments are due at six-month intervals within the fiscal year.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Final corporate tax return must be filed within three months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year taxpayer the deadline is March 31 of the next year; non-resident corporations may, through a tax representative, obtain an NTS extension of up to seven months after fiscal year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate identification: legal name, business registration number, tax residence indicator, and branch/head-office classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean registration number of Yuhan Hoesa and disclose the ultimate foreign parent name and country of residence. Attach the foreign certificate of incorporation, Korean branch registration, and foreign tax identification number; the information must match the Foreign Exchange and Transaction Act report for outbound remittance.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reportable gross revenue under Korean IFRS, including export sales of laser-micro-machined coronary drug-eluting stents and related services.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Classify export shipments to related distributors by destination jurisdiction and customs entry; apply OECD treaty article 7 for business profits if the foreign principal has no Korean PE, and article 12 for royalty income if the payment is for technology or licensing; attach the invoice-level export schedule to support local filing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 20 / Deductions, COGS, and Transfer Pricing Adjustments
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Cost of goods sold, operating expenses, intercompany charges, and transfer pricing adjustments for the taxable year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All deductible intercompany payments must be supported by an arm's-length Local File. Royalty and service charges paid to non-residents are deductible only if the payee has actual personnel, premises, functions, and business substance; disallowed amounts are recharacterized as invisible dividends and subjected to 22% withholding.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 26 / Tax Loss Carryforwards and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net operating loss deductions carried forward and credits for foreign income taxes paid or withheld.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Korea permits a 15-year NOL carryforward for corporations; the schedule must identify the fiscal year of each carried loss and any 60% taxable income limitation. Foreign tax credits are available only for Korean-source income where treaty rate claims do not exceed the amount actually paid.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 34 / Withholding and Non-Resident Tax Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Summary of Korean-source income paid to non-residents and the withholding tax due under Corporate Tax Act Article 98 and Local Tax Act Article 103.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report outbound dividends, interest, and royalties separately. Apply the statutory 22% combined WHT unless an NTS treaty reduction has been approved; attach the payee tax residency certificate, beneficial ownership declaration, and treaty application approval number. An unapproved or late treaty claim may be denied and additional penalties assessed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing under Corporate Tax Act Article 76 adds 20% to fraudulent underreported tax and 10% for ordinary underreported or unpaid tax; unpaid tax accrues daily late-payment interest at approximately 0.022%; failure to withhold non-resident tax triggers a 3% monthly withholding penalty up to a 9.5% annual cap; criminal fraud under the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act can lead to imprisonment and fines up to five times the tax evaded, with NTS blacklisting of the entity and its representative.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate for a non-resident corporation receiving dividends from a Korean payer (20% corporate income withholding under Corporate Tax Act Article 98 plus 2% local income tax surtax under Local Tax Act Article 103).
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a lower DTA rate, the non-resident beneficiary must (1) obtain an active-record Tax Residency Certificate from the treaty jurisdiction, (2) file a written Application for Tax Treaty Exemption or Reduction with the withholding agent or National Tax Service before the withholding due date, (3) provide a signed beneficial ownership declaration proving the recipient is the actual owner of the dividend, interest, or royalty, and (4) demonstrate business substance if the treaty contains a principal purpose test or limitation-on-benefits clause. NTS approval is recorded in the HomeTax system; if treaty relief is denied at source, the non-resident may pay the tax and file a refund claim within three years or initiate the Mutual Agreement Procedure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 22% (20% national plus 2% local); DTA reductions are generally 10 to 15%, with modern treaties adopting 10% for certain royalties and Article 12 OECD treatment. Interest: statutory 22%; DTA reductions are generally 10 to 15%, with 0% available only to government-related lenders under specific treaty articles. Intercompany interest is also subject to Korea thin-capitalization rules, generally disallowing interest on related-party debt exceeding a 2:1 debt-to-equity ratio for foreign-affiliated lenders.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is required when aggregate cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion in the taxable year, with simplified documentation available above KRW 10 billion for small and medium-sized enterprises; Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion and Korean related-party cross-border transactions exceeding KRW 50 billion; Country-by-Country Report filing is mandatory when the group has consolidated revenue of at least KRW 1 trillion.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not have a formal Economic Substance Regulations regime but applies substance-over-form under the Corporate Tax Act, the Act on International Tax Adjustment, and controlled foreign corporation rules. To preserve treaty benefits and avoid recharacterization, the Korean stent manufacturing entity must perform core income-generating activities in Korea: laser micro-machining, polymer processing, cleanroom assembly, sterilization, quality assurance, regulatory licensing, warehousing, and hospital distribution logistics; a foreign shell company may not book returns without employees, premises, inventory, and risk-bearing functions in the jurisdiction.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion and fictitious invoicing in medical-device exports
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining two revenue ledgers for drug-eluting stent exports, issuing fictitious export invoices to a non-resident distributor, or under-invoicing exports so that Korean taxable profit is diverted to an offshore account.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 3 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act and Corporate Tax Act Article 76 apply: income is reassessed on true export revenue, a 20% fraudulent underreporting penalty applies, daily late-payment interest accrues, a Value-Added Tax penalty is imposed on fake export invoices, and criminal fines can reach five times the tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: A court may pierce the corporate veil under Korean Civil Code and Commercial Act Article 401; directors who signed false invoices are jointly and severally liable for the company unpaid tax and penalties, may be placed on the NTS high-risk blacklist, may face overseas travel bans for unpaid tax over KRW 100 million, and may receive imprisonment of up to three years for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing manipulation by relocating stent patent rights to a low-tax affiliate
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Transferring the bioresorbable vascular polymer stent patent to a zero or low-tax jurisdiction affiliate for a one-off valuation that is not arm's length, then paying an excessive royalty back to Korea while Korean management and R&D staff continue performing core development functions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The National Tax Service may adjust the royalty deduction, recharacterize excessive payments as dividends, apply the OECD approved transfer pricing methods, impose a 20% underreporting penalty, and assess a documentation failure penalty under Act on International Tax Adjustment Article 35 if the Local File or benchmark study is missing or false.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Controlling directors are jointly and severally obligated under Commercial Act Article 401 and may be prosecuted for fraudulent concealment of related-party transactions; they can be personally assessed for the corporation tax arrears, blacklisted with NTS, subject to exit bans, and imprisoned for up to three years where willful misvaluation is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding tax evasion on outbound dividends and royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing a dividend to a non-resident shareholder without withholding the 22% statutory WHT, or labeling a royalty payment as an export service fee to the offshore parent in order to avoid the 22% withholding on royalties, while failing to file for treaty relief or falsely claiming treaty benefits without beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The withholding agent and the Korean payer are jointly liable for the unpaid corporate income tax and local surtax under Corporate Tax Act Article 98 and Local Tax Act Article 103; a 3% monthly withholding failure penalty applies up to the 9.5% annual cap, daily late-payment interest runs, and the DTA reduction is denied where the recipient is not the beneficial owner.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who authorized the payment or received the funds are personally liable for the corporation withholding tax debt as joint tax obligors, lose NTS leniency eligibility, face travel restrictions, and are criminally prosecuted under Article 10 of the Punishment of Tax Offenses Act with imprisonment up to three years or a fine up to five times the unpaid withholding tax.
